author: reek
body: `keys-sidecar` pins the base path -- a key arrives and is translated. This pins the part `keys-sidecar` deliberately does not touch: the shift latch. A keyboard hands you the modifier and the key as separate events, so `poll-key` watches a shift make code set a latch cell and the matching break code clear it, and cases every letter and symbol in between.

author: reek
body: So the three collected codes must be **65, 97, 33**: `A` (shifted lower), `a` (unshifted), `!` (shift+1). A latch that never set would give 97, 97, 49; one that never cleared would give 65, 65, 33. Only a latch that both sets and clears yields this sequence, which is what makes it a test of the latch rather than of either half alone.

author: reek
body: No fuel cap, on purpose, the same as `keys-sidecar`: a key that never arrives must hang and be failed by the wall budget, not pass on a truncated answer.
